$schema_note: Reference-only extraction from the Benchwarmers 2026/27 spreadsheet model. Read-only, formulas + cached values as of the timestamps below. This does not imply spreadsheet parity is implemented in Python yet.

calc_properties.note: fullCalcOnLoad=true means Excel would recalculate everything on next open in Excel. Values extracted here are openpyxl's cached (last-saved) results, read without opening/recalculating in Excel, so they reflect whatever state the file was saved in.

MODEL.xlsx.role: Primary source for MODEL and PPts sheet formulas used in this extraction.

SOLVER.xlsx.role: Downstream squad-optimizer workbook. Not a source of appearance/minutes formulas; not used in this extraction.

SIMPLE MODEL.xlsx.role: Simplified/derivative workbook without the MODEL/PPts sheets. Not used in this extraction.

control_assumptions.note: Values as cached/saved in MODEL.xlsx. These are user-editable blend weights, not hardcoded model constants.

last_gw_pre_season_marker.meaning: 0 means the workbook is currently in preseason (no current-season GW has been played yet).

1_60_mins_blend.label: 1-60 mins: Previous Season vs This Season weight
1_60_mins_blend.effect: With B8=1, B9=0, the '1' (appearance) column is currently driven 100% by previous-season PS %1 and 0% by this-season %1.

60_plus_mins_blend.label: 60+ mins: Previous Season vs This Season weight
60_plus_mins_blend.effect: With B19=1, B20=0, the '2' (60-minute) column is currently driven 100% by previous-season PS %2 and 0% by this-season %2.

mn_st_trend_table.label: Mn/St lookup table used by CW/CX (PS %2 / %2) TREND() interpolation
columns: C = % below 60 minutes at that Mn/St
mn_st_trend_table.usage: MATCH(Mn/St, B13:B17, -1) finds the bracket (descending lookup), then TREND() linearly interpolates the '% below 60' fraction between the two bracketing points. If Mn/St < 50, the fallback constant 0.5 is used directly instead of TREND().

defensive_contributions_short_form_windo.note: CONTROL!B84 (Short Form Length=10), C84, D84, E84, and CONTROL!E2 (current GW column match) feed the SF DC columns (CN:CQ). These are DefCon inputs, out of scope for this extraction, included only because CP2 formula reads them.

columns_CR_to_CY.note: All formulas below are identical (structured-table references) across every data row observed (spot-checked rows 2-5, 100, 500, 799). CR and CV are the only two of this block that are literal constants, not formulas.

CR.meaning: Fixed weight/marker, not a formula. Always 1 for every row.

CS.formula: =IF(AND(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Starts]]=0,MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Subs]]=0),0.01,(1-MODEL[[#This Row],[PS UnSub/SqdsMd]])*0.99)
CS.meaning: Previous-season probability of a 1-60-minute appearance. If the player had zero previous-season starts AND zero previous-season subs, hardcode 0.01 (near-zero prior). Otherwise, (1 - PS UnSub/SqdsMd) * 0.99, i.e. 99% times the complement of the 'named in squad but did not play' rate.

CT.meaning: Same logic as CS but using this-season Starts/Subs/UnSub/SqdsMd. During preseason (no GWs played) this-season Starts/Subs are always 0, so this always evaluates to the 0.01 fallback.

CU.formula: =IFERROR(((MODEL[[#This Row],[PS %1]]*CONTROL!$B$8)+(MODEL[[#This Row],[%1]]*CONTROL!$B$9))*MODEL[[#This Row],[1-60 mins]]*MODEL[[#This Row],[Chance of Playing]],0)
CU.meaning: Blended appearance probability = (PS%1 * previous-season weight + %1 * this-season weight) * CR('1-60 mins' constant, always 1) * Chance of Playing (API-sourced fitness flag, defaults to 1 if blank). Wrapped in IFERROR->0.

CV.meaning: Fixed weight/marker, not a formula. Always 1 for every row, structurally mirrors CR.

CW.formula:
=IFERROR((0.98-IF(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Mn/St]]<50,0.5,TREND(
  INDEX(CONTROL!$C$13:$C$17,MATCH(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Mn/St]],CONTROL!$B$13:$B$17,-1)):INDEX(CONTROL!$C$13:$C$17,MATCH(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Mn/St]],CONTROL!$B$13:$B$17,-1)+1),
  INDEX(CONTROL!$B$13:$B$17,MATCH(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Mn/St]],CONTROL!$B$13:$B$17,-1)):INDEX(CONTROL!$B$13:$B$17,MATCH(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Mn/St]],CONTROL!$B$13:$B$17,-1)+1),
  MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Mn/St]]
))),0)
CW.meaning: Previous-season probability of reaching 60 minutes GIVEN a start, derived as 0.98 minus an interpolated 'chance of being subbed before 60 mins' curve keyed on PS Mn/St (average minutes per previous-season start), using the CONTROL!B13:C17 lookup table. If PS Mn/St < 50, uses a flat 0.5 penalty instead of interpolating.

CX.meaning: This-season analogue of CW, using this-season Mn/St. Base constant is 0.99 (vs 0.98 for PS %2) -- a spreadsheet quirk (see quirks). During preseason, this-season Mn/St is 0, which is <50, so this always uses the flat 0.5 penalty branch: result = 0.99 - 0.5 = 0.49.

CY.meaning: Blended 60+ minute probability (given the player plays) = (PS%2 * previous-season weight + %2 * this-season weight) * CV('60+ mins' constant, always 1). Unlike CU, this has no explicit IFERROR wrapper and no Chance-of-Playing multiplication -- Chance of Playing is not applied to column '2' at the MODEL sheet level.

PS_Starts_J.source_chain: EO (Previous Season Starts1) <- dedupe of EK:EN, which are 4 parallel name-matched lookups (FPL_Name/web_name/FBRef_Name/Alt Name 2) into PSPT[Starts].

PS_Subs_K.source_chain: FI (Subs1... for PS this is a separate 'Previous Season Subs1' column using the same EO-style dedupe pattern against PSPT[Subs].

PS_UnSub_L.source_chain: Dedupe of 4 name-matched lookups against PSPT[unSub].

PS_Mn_St_M.source_chain: FS <- dedupe of FO:FR name-matched lookups against PSPT.

PS_Mn_Sub_N.source_chain: GC <- dedupe of FY:GB name-matched lookups against PSPT.

PS_Mn_St_pct_O.meaning: Goalkeepers assumed to play full 90 if they start (1.0). Outfield players with zero previous-season starts default to 0.66 (66% of 90 = 59.4 min, just under the 60-min threshold). Otherwise PS Mn/St / 90.

PS_Mn_Sub_pct_P.meaning: Default substitute cameo assumption of 0.2 (18 minutes) when there is no previous-season substitute-minutes data.

PS_Sts_SqdsMd_Q.formula: =IFERROR(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Starts]]/(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Starts]]+MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Subs]]+MODEL[[#This Row],[PS UnSub]]),0)
PS_Sts_SqdsMd_Q.meaning: Previous-season starts as a fraction of all squad involvements (start+sub+unused-sub).

PS_UnSub_SqdsMd_R.formula: =IFERROR(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS UnSub]]/(MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Starts]]+MODEL[[#This Row],[PS Subs]]+MODEL[[#This Row],[PS UnSub]]),0)
PS_UnSub_SqdsMd_R.meaning: Previous-season 'named but never got on' rate as a fraction of all squad involvements.

Chance_of_Playing_AM.meaning: Pulled from official FPL API 'chance_of_playing_next_round' (0-100 integer, blank if fully fit). Blank -> 1.0 (fully available). Otherwise divided by 100 to get a 0-1 fraction. IFERROR->0 catches unmatched codes.

Starts_AN.source_chain: This-season analogue of PS Starts, deduped against PT (not PSPT).

appearance_and_minutes_fields.dedupe_pattern_note: Starts1/Subs1/UnSub1/Mn-Start1/Mn-Sub1 (and their 'Previous Season ...' counterparts) are each built from 4 parallel name-matched lookups (FPL_Name, web_name, FBRef_Name, Alt Name 2) against a source table (PT for this-season, PSPT for previous-season). The dedupe formula sums all 4 lookups, then IF the sum equals any single one of the 4 values (i.e. only one lookup actually matched, the rest returned 0), uses the sum as-is; otherwise divides by 2. This assumes at most 2 of the 4 name variants can simultaneously match a real row, and divides by 2 to undo double-counting when exactly 2 match. This heuristic would silently miscount if 3 or 4 of the aliases matched simultaneously.

AY_PRE_HA_TOTAL.formula: =PPts[[#This Row],[1-60 mins]]+PPts[[#This Row],[2]]+PPts[[#This Row],[3]]+PPts[[#This Row],[4]]+PPts[[#This Row],[5]]+PPts[[#This Row],[6]]+PPts[[#This Row],[7]]+PPts[[#This Row],[8]]+PPts[[#This Row],[9]]+PPts[[#This Row],[10]]+PPts[[#This Row],[11]]
AY_PRE_HA_TOTAL.meaning: Sum of all 11 component xPts columns (appearance, 60-min, saves, cards, bonus, assists, goals, clean sheets, goals-conceded, DC) before any home/away adjustment. Included for context; not itself in BA:BI but feeds BA.

AZ_HA.meaning: Home/away multiplier. VS is the opponent abbreviation; it is stored UPPERCASE for a home fixture and lowercase for an away fixture (see PPts!Q formula), so EXACT(VS, UPPER(VS)) is a case-sensitive test for 'is this string already uppercase' i.e. 'is this a home fixture'. Home -> 1.05, Away -> 0.95.

BA.meaning: Zero if there is no valid fixture this row (VS resolves to '-' or blank, length <3). Otherwise PRE H/A TOTAL * H/A: the full component sum, home/away-adjusted once. This is the 'expected points assuming the player starts' figure, before minutes-blending with the not-start branch.

BB.meaning: Blended (Previous-Season weight * PS Sts/SqdsMd) + (This-Season weight * St/SqdsMd), reusing the CONTROL!B8/B9 weights from the MODEL sheet's '1-60 mins' blend. This is effectively the model's estimate of P(start | named in squad).

BC.formula: =IF(INDEX(PREDICT[Manual Start %],MATCH(PPts[[#This Row],[Code]],PREDICT[HARD CODE],0))="","",INDEX(PREDICT[Manual Start %],MATCH(PPts[[#This Row],[Code]],PREDICT[HARD CODE],0)))
BC.meaning: Pass-through of a hand-entered override from PREDICT!H (Manual Start %), keyed by player code (PREDICT!B, HARD CODE). Empty string when no manual override exists for that player. This is a manual/analyst input, not a derived value.

BD.meaning: Direct lookup of the MODEL sheet's blended appearance-probability column '1' (MODEL!CU) for this player.

BE.formula: =IF(PPts[[#This Row],[M Start %]]="",PPts[[#This Row],[MODEL 1]],(1*PPts[[#This Row],[M Start %]])+((1-PPts[[#This Row],[M Start %]])*PPts[[#This Row],[MODEL 1]]))
BE.meaning: SEE QUIRKS: when no manual override, T1 = MODEL 1 (a 0-1 probability). When a manual override IS present, T1 = (1 * M_Start%) + ((1 - M_Start%) * MODEL_1). This blends M_Start% as if it were itself a points value (weight 1, not P(start)-weighted), added to a shrunk residual of MODEL 1. It is NOT a probability-weighted average of two probabilities; the resulting T1 can exceed either input (see Saka golden case: M_Start%=0.6, MODEL_1=0.9590625 -> T1=0.983625, greater than both).

BF.meaning: Ratio of blended expected substitute minutes to blended expected starting minutes for this player (goals+assists blend columns AK/AL on MODEL, reused here as a generic minutes-scaling ratio). Used to scale down the 'if not start' component total to reflect a substitute's reduced minutes versus a starter's.

BG.formula: =((PPts[[#This Row],[4]]+PPts[[#This Row],[5]]+PPts[[#This Row],[6]]+PPts[[#This Row],[7]]+PPts[[#This Row],[8]]+PPts[[#This Row],[10]])*PPts[[#This Row],[PSxTS Mn/Sub / Mn/St]]*PPts[[#This Row],[H/A]])
BG.meaning: Sum of only the rate-scalable component columns (4,5,6,7,8,10 -- cards/bonus/assists/goals/DC; explicitly EXCLUDES columns 2 '60+ mins', 3 '3x Saves', 9 'CS', and 11 which are either start-gated or non-linear in minutes) times the Mn/Sub-to-Mn/Start ratio (scaling starter-based rates down to substitute-cameo minutes) times H/A. SEE QUIRKS: H/A is applied here.

BH.formula: =IF(PPts[[#This Row],[M Start %]]<>"",PPts[[#This Row],[M Start %]],INDEX(MODEL[Chance of Playing],MATCH(PPts[[#This Row],[Code]],MODEL[Code],0))*PPts[[#This Row],[PSxTS Starts/Squads Made]])
BH.meaning: The actual probability weight used to blend BA (start branch) and BG (not-start branch) in BI. Uses the manual override directly if present, otherwise Chance of Playing * PSxTS Starts/Squads Made. Note this is a genuine 0-1 probability, unlike T1 (BE) which is not.

BI.formula: =IF(LEN(PPts[[#This Row],[VS]])<3,0,(PPts[[#This Row],[T1]]+((PPts[[#This Row],[2]]+PPts[[#This Row],[3]]+PPts[[#This Row],[4]]+PPts[[#This Row],[5]]+PPts[[#This Row],[6]]+PPts[[#This Row],[7]]+PPts[[#This Row],[8]]+PPts[[#This Row],[9]]+PPts[[#This Row],[10]]+PPts[[#This Row],[11]])*PPts[[#This Row],[Start %]])+(PPts[[#This Row],[IF NOT START TOTAL]]*(1-PPts[[#This Row],[Start %]])))*PPts[[#This Row],[H/A]])
BI.meaning: SEE QUIRKS (H/A double-application). Final per-fixture expected points = 0 if no valid fixture. Otherwise: [T1 (quirky start-branch appearance term, NOT itself H/A-adjusted) + (full component sum 2..11 * Start%, i.e. an expected-value blend using the *other* start-probability BH) + (BG not-start branch, which ALREADY has H/A baked in, * (1-Start%))] all multiplied by H/A again.

expected_outputs.note: With Start %=1, BI collapses to (T1 + full_sum*1)*H/A = (T1+full_sum)*H/A since the not-start branch is weighted by (1-1)=0, so the H/A double-application quirk is invisible for this player -- a useful check case precisely because it ISOLATES the pure start branch.

Verified by hand: BI = (T1 + sum(cols 2..11)*Start% + BG*(1-Start%)) * H/A = (0.9639473684210527 + 3.3524791064486017*0.5 + 0.7740236578188885*0.5) * 1.05 = 3.1785586880825383, matching cache to full float precision. This confirms the H/A-applied-twice mechanism reproducibly (BG already includes one H/A factor internally).

PS Mn/St=60 exactly hits the CONTROL!B16=60 breakpoint (C16=0.5), so CW379 = 0.98-0.5 = 0.48 without needing TREND() interpolation -- a useful edge-of-table check. Start%=0.0278 means TRUE TOTAL is dominated almost entirely by the not-start branch (subs cameo scaling), not the start branch, unlike Raya/Barnes.

SPREADSHEET QUIRK: PS Starts=0 AND PS Subs=0 (46 unused-sub appearances only) triggers the CS 'AND(...=0,...=0)' branch giving PS%1=0.01, a near-zero-but-not-zero appearance prior. Start%=0 makes TRUE TOTAL collapse to BG*(1-0)*H/A = BG*H/A = -0.0820487146432367*0.95 = -0.06844627891107487, a NEGATIVE expected-points figure for a permanent benchwarmer, because BG's card/bonus/assist/goal/DC component sum for this GK happens to be slightly negative (dominated by a negative '4' cards component) before scaling. This is a genuine spreadsheet artifact worth flagging, not a modelling choice worth reproducing as-is.

PRIMARY EXAMPLE for the T1 manual-start-formula quirk (see quirks). Included specifically because PREDICT!H24 has a clean, human-entered Manual Start % (0.6) so the quirky blend formula in BE is directly verifiable by hand, unlike the 4 core golden cases above where M Start % is blank and T1 trivially equals MODEL 1.

warnings.detail: MODEL.xlsx has calculation.fullCalcOnLoad=True, meaning Excel would recompute all formulas the next time a human opens and saves the file. openpyxl's data_only=True reads only whatever values were cached at last save; this extraction did NOT open the file in Excel and therefore reflects that last-saved cache, which could differ from a fresh recalculation if any upstream source sheet (API, PT, PSPT, MINS, DC, FIXHELPER) changed since the last save without the workbook being reopened and saved in Excel.

Rows 2-800 of MODEL (799 data rows) and rows 2-2000 of PPts (per-player GW1 rows only) were scanned for missing/error values in the columns used by this extraction (Chance of Playing, Starts, '1', '2', PS %1, %1, PS %2, %2). Zero None/error values were found in that range. Rows beyond 800 in MODEL, and non-GW1 rows in PPts, were not exhaustively scanned for staleness.

CONTROL!B3 = 0 ('LAST GW (Pre-Season = 0)') and CONTROL!B8=1/B9=0, B19=1/B20=0 mean the workbook, as extracted, is 100% previous-season-weighted for both the appearance ('1') and 60-minute ('2') columns. This-season Starts/Subs/UnSub/Mn-St/Mn-Sub are all 0 for every player at this point in the season, so '%1' and '%2' (this-season columns) are always at their fallback constants (0.01 and 0.49 respectively) and contribute nothing numerically even though B9/B20 are nonzero in general. Any reference outputs extracted here are therefore a preseason snapshot, not representative of in-season blending behavior once B3 advances past 0.

MODEL!Starts1/Subs1/UnSub1/Mn-Start1/Mn-Sub1 (and PS equivalents) depend on a 4-way name-matching dedupe against PT/PSPT sheets, which were not individually audited row-by-row in this extraction beyond confirming the dedupe formula's structure. If a player's FPL_Name/web_name/FBRef_Name/Alt Name 2 aliases produce 3+ simultaneous matches against PT/PSPT, the /2 correction in the dedupe formula would silently undercount -- not verified either way for the 4 golden-case players.

spreadsheet_quirks.title: CR ('1-60 mins') and CV ('60+ mins') are literal 1s, not formulas
spreadsheet_quirks.detail: Despite sharing a header row with formula-driven probability columns, MODEL!CR and MODEL!CV contain the hardcoded literal value 1 in every data row (spot-checked rows 2, 3, 4, 5, 100, 500, 799). They function purely as fixed multipliers inside CU and CY (effectively no-ops at their current value) rather than as computed scenario weights. If a future spreadsheet revision changed these to real formulas, CU/CY's meaning would change; as-is, they can be treated as always-1 constants.

spreadsheet_quirks.title: T1's manual-start blend is not a probability-weighted average
spreadsheet_quirks.detail: PPts!BE (T1) = IF(M_Start%="", MODEL_1, (1*M_Start%) + ((1-M_Start%)*MODEL_1)). When a manual override is present, this adds M_Start% at full weight (coefficient 1, not M_Start%) to a (1-M_Start%)-shrunk MODEL_1, rather than computing anything resembling P(start)-weighted expected value of two probabilities. Verified on Bukayo Saka (golden case 'manual_start_override_example'): M_Start%=0.6, MODEL_1=0.9590625 -> T1=0.983625, a value greater than either input. T1 feeds only the start-branch numerator in BI; the actual probability used to WEIGHT the start vs not-start branches is the separate BH (Start %) column, which IS a clean probability (uses M_Start% directly when present). So the spreadsheet has two different uses of 'manual start %' in the same row: one as a direct probability weight (BH) and one folded into a non-probabilistic point-boost formula (T1/BE). Any Python reproduction must decide deliberately whether to replicate this asymmetry or treat it as a bug to fix.

spreadsheet_quirks.title: H/A (home/away multiplier) is applied twice to the non-start branch's contribution to TRUE TOTAL
spreadsheet_quirks.detail: PPts!BG (IF NOT START TOTAL) = (sum of components 4,5,6,7,8,10) * (Mn/Sub-to-Mn/Start ratio) * H/A -- one H/A factor baked in. PPts!BI (TRUE TOTAL) = (T1 + full_sum*Start% + BG*(1-Start%)) * H/A -- wraps the ENTIRE blended total, including the already-H/A-adjusted BG, in a second H/A multiplication. Verified by hand on Harvey Barnes (golden case 'rotation_prone_starter'): BG=0.7740236578188885 already includes one factor of H/A=1.05 (BG recomputed without H/A = 0.7371653883989414; 0.7371653883989414*1.05 = 0.7740236578188885, matching cache). The T1 term and the full_sum*Start% term are each only H/A-adjusted once (via the outer multiplication), so the double-application is specific to the not-start branch. Net effect: the home/away adjustment is slightly overstated for players with meaningful (1-Start%) substitute-cameo weight, more so for extreme home/away fixtures (H/A=1.05 or 0.95 compounds to 1.1025 or 0.9025 on that portion). This is very likely an unintentional spreadsheet bug rather than a deliberate design choice, since there is no equivalent second H/A factor anywhere in the start-branch path.

spreadsheet_quirks.title: TRUE TOTAL can be negative for permanent non-appearance players
spreadsheet_quirks.detail: For a player with Start%=0 (e.g. Ben Wilson, golden case 'likely_non_appearance'), TRUE TOTAL collapses to BG*H/A alone. BG sums components 4 (cards, can be negative in this model), 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 scaled by the Mn/Sub-to-Mn/Start ratio; for Wilson this sum is slightly negative (-0.0820487146432367 after H/A), producing TRUE TOTAL = -0.06844627891107487 -- a small negative expected-points value for a player who essentially never plays. A points model conventionally floors expected points at 0; this spreadsheet does not, at least not in this column.

spreadsheet_quirks.title: PS %2 uses base constant 0.98, %2 (this-season) uses 0.99
spreadsheet_quirks.detail: MODEL!CW (PS %2) formula is '=IFERROR((0.98-IF(...` while MODEL!CX (%2) is '=IFERROR((0.99-IF(...'. Both otherwise share identical structure (same CONTROL!B13:C17 TREND lookup, same <50-minutes fallback of 0.5). The 0.98 vs 0.99 base constant is not explained anywhere in CONTROL and is not parameterized -- it is hardcoded per-formula. Unclear whether this is intentional (e.g. previous-season data assumed slightly noisier / capped 1% lower) or a copy-paste inconsistency. Flagged as an ambiguity, not resolved by this extraction.

spreadsheet_quirks.title: The zero-appearance-history fallback for PS %1 / %1 is 0.01, not exactly 0
spreadsheet_quirks.detail: MODEL!CS / CT: IF(Starts=0 AND Subs=0, 0.01, (1-UnSub/SqdsMd)*0.99). A player with truly zero previous appearances (no starts, no subs, regardless of UnSub count) gets a nonzero 1% prior appearance probability rather than 0. This is a deliberate Bayesian-style prior (never fully rule out an appearance) but is worth flagging explicitly since it means MODEL!'1' is never exactly 0 for any player with Chance of Playing > 0, even one who has never played a single previous-season minute (see also Chelsea's Quenda/Emegha in the wider scan, both showing '1'=0.0075 = 0.01*0.75 Chance-of-Playing).
